motivo: Día de primer número del diario, con mucha charla sobre la propia publicación (descartada). Quedan una pauta práctica sobre infografías, un informe del MIT, un debate sobre el papel docente, una pauta de seguridad con agentes de consola y un recurso de vídeo.

piezas.titular: A teacher recommends building infographics in HTML and SVG rather than as generated images
piezas.entradilla: A member of Vibe Coding Educativo argues that, to illustrate concepts, AI should generate SVG shapes and icons in an HTML page, with generated images kept for when they are pedagogically necessary.
cuerpo: The proposal came up in a discussion of using vector illustrations instead of AI-generated images. Its author recommends asking AI to build the infographic as an HTML page with SVG shapes and a single family of icons, checking it thoroughly and, if needed, exporting it to PNG afterwards.

The advantages listed include sharpness; control for whoever creates it; consistency across resources, which makes it possible to set a shared “style book”; accessibility, because a screen reader can read the text of an HTML infographic but not that of an image without a description; and automatic adaptation to light and dark modes. HTML also supports collapsible components that reveal information in stages, which, in this view, helps avoid cognitive overload and adds a degree of interactivity.

Members also advised steering clear of infographics overloaded with decorative elements, generating images only when the teaching objective requires it, and always crediting the chosen icon family. [Lucide](https://lucide.dev/), mentioned in the group, is an open-source set of SVG icons released under the ISC licence.
For teachers, the practical takeaway is knowing when an editable, accessible infographic is the better choice and when a generated image is.
piezas.comprobado: Lucide (lucide.dev), abierta por el revisor: indica «Released under the ISC License»; en el grupo se dijo MIT y no se recoge. Mensaje 14501 de t.me/vceduca verificado: trata de imágenes SVG con formas e iconos. Las ventajas y recomendaciones son opinión expresada en el grupo y se presentan como tal; no se abrió el capítulo académico ni la documentación de Bootstrap enlazados allí. Titular corregido: es la recomendación de un miembro, no de «docentes».
piezas.ilustracion: Esquema de dos caminos desde una idea: a la izquierda una imagen generada (un bloque opaco, sin texto leíble ni modo oscuro); a la derecha una infografía HTML/SVG hecha de formas e iconos, con etiquetas de «texto legible por lector de pantalla», «modo claro/oscuro» y «exportable a PNG».
piezas.ilustracion_alt: Diagram in which an “Idea” splits into two paths: one ends in a crossed-out opaque block, the “Generated image”, and the other in an infographic of shapes and icons, “HTML and SVG”, from which two advantages branch off: “Screen reader” and “Light and dark”.

piezas.titular: MIT report calls for rethinking teaching and assessment in the age of AI
piezas.entradilla: The committee set up by MIT to study the use of AI in teaching, learning and research training recommends AI-aware educational processes and a review of assessments and policies.
cuerpo: The report of MIT’s Ad Hoc Committee on the use of AI in teaching, learning and research training was shared in ChatGPT-IA-edu. According to MIT’s institutional page, the committee was commissioned in January 2026 and its final report was released on 25 August 2026.

The text proposes immediate and longer-term action along three lines: creating AI-aware educational processes, which means reviewing what students should learn and how they should achieve it, with changes to assessments and policies; keeping people, community and the on-campus experience at the centre; and putting in place the processes, teams and tools for continuous improvement, given the pace of change in AI. The institution also says that faculty will receive guidance for drafting their own AI policies.
For teachers at other levels, it is a reference for how a major university is tackling the issue: by reviewing assessment and policies rather than simply banning.

fuentes.titulo: MIT: statement on the report of the Ad Hoc Committee on AI

piezas.comprobado: Página del MIT (orgchart.mit.edu/node/1587), abierta por el revisor: informe final del 25 de agosto de 2026, comité encargado en enero de 2026, las tres líneas de recomendación y las orientaciones al profesorado para sus normas. Mensaje 53877 de t.me/ChatGPTedu verificado. Se quitó la afirmación de que se recomienda fijar reglas por asignatura y departamento, que la página no recoge, y se ajustó el titular de la fuente. El PDF del informe no se leyó.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: A “Report” from which three branches extend, each with its own icon: a sheet with a tick, “Assessment and rules”; two people, “People and campus”; and two arrows in a circle, “Continuous improvement”.

piezas.titular: Teachers as designers of learning are at the heart of the debate on AI in the classroom
piezas.entradilla: After a conference on AI and education, members ask whether teachers stop being a source of information and how to prevent students from delegating their reasoning.
cuerpo: One view holds that teaching and learning is undergoing a paradigm shift: teachers become designers of learning and guides, no longer the origin of information. Those who share it say they are concerned that students may delegate their reasoning to AI and that critical judgement, reflection and problem-solving need to be fostered.

Another contribution, in favour of that shift, frames it as a question for those who teach: do lessons spark enough curiosity for students not to turn to AI by default, and would it not be more fruitful to start from a research question than from an explanation followed by copying? It adds that AI is already a source of information for many teachers and companies, so what matters would be teaching students to discern critically.

A third contribution points out that, if students are going to live in a world with AI, they should already be preparing for it, and anticipates an interest in an “ethical agentic engineering” approach from an educational perspective. One of the contributions also raises a dilemma: using AI to create content while restricting it in students’ tasks.
piezas.comprobado: Pieza de opinión: recoge posturas expresadas en el grupo (mensajes 53855, 53865, 53871, 53873, 53874), sin nombres y sin afirmaciones sobre productos, cifras ni normas. Mensaje 53855 de t.me/ChatGPTedu verificado. Titular y entradilla corregidos: no hubo división de posturas, sino matices sobre un mismo planteamiento. No se incluyen las comparaciones con experiencias de otros países, no contrastadas.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: On the left, “Source”: a teacher transmits information with arrows towards three students; on the right, “Designer and guide”: another teacher with a question mark designs a route of stages leading to a flag labelled “Critical judgement”.

piezas.titular: Giving a command-line agent full access means protecting students’ data
piezas.entradilla: An experienced teacher explained what an AI agent with full control of a computer can do and what information should be kept out of its reach.
cuerpo: Asked what to consider before giving a command-line agent control of a computer, one member replied that with full access it can move and delete files, change settings, and install or uninstall programs. That capability is what makes it so versatile: in one case described, the agent built a complete project on a NAS from scratch and unaided, including obtaining a GitHub key to upload it.

The main caution concerns data. Students’ data is especially well protected and should not reach AI servers without knowing exactly what is being done and without the necessary permissions. Bank accounts and highly sensitive personal information are best kept separate. According to the person explaining, the agent itself can advise on how to protect that data from itself.

It was also noted that the agent can be restricted to a specific folder rather than the whole device, and an updated text was announced on the three ways of using AI: web, desktop app and command line.
piezas.comprobado: Consejos y experiencia relatados en el grupo (mensajes 14542, 14544-14546), sin afirmaciones técnicas sobre un producto concreto; contrastados con el texto del chat. Mensaje 14542 de t.me/vceduca verificado: es la pregunta sobre dar control a una consola. No se enlaza el artículo mencionado porque no se ha abierto.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: A terminal window, the agent, has an arrow towards a working folder inside a computer, while its path to the students’ data folder, marked with a padlock, is cut off by a red cross.

piezas.titular: A website gathers motion-graphics videos with their prompts and skills for agents
piezas.entradilla: MotionVideo offers AI-made videos accompanied by their prompts, and skills that teach a coding agent how to do motion design.
cuerpo: [motionvideo.xyz](https://motionvideo.xyz/en), a website of AI-made motion-graphics videos, was shared in EduMedia-IAG. Each video is published with its prompt, and the site also offers skills, reusable instructions that teach a coding agent motion design, with a link to GitHub. The videos are grouped by type, such as kinetic typography, charts, diagrams, particles and music.

A member of the group said they had adapted a skill designed for Claude to Gemini and, with a two-line prompt and a video from the site as a reference, produced the title sequence for a theatre teaser. This is a personal experience that could not be verified.
For teachers, the interest lies in having examples with their prompts for producing short introductory videos or videos that support an explanation.
piezas.comprobado: Página de motionvideo.xyz, abierta por el revisor: vídeos con su prompt, técnicas, skills para agentes, enlace a GitHub y categorías (Kinetic type, Charts, Diagrams, Particles, Music, entre otras). Mensaje 11986 de t.me/EduMediaIAG verificado. La prueba con Gemini es un relato del grupo y se presenta como tal.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: Three boxes linked by arrows: a written prompt, a skill shaped like a terminal window, and a video with a play button and a red motion path beneath it.

breves.texto: The website for Ethan Mollick’s new book includes an “AI cursor” that accompanies the reading and can be switched off. Members rated it as an idea for popularising the subject.

repaso: Infografías: titular de «Docentes recomiendan» a «Un docente recomienda» (era un solo miembro); «según esta opinión» en la ventaja de los componentes plegables.

MIT: quitada la afirmación, no recogida por la fuente, de que se recomienda que cada docente y departamento fije cuándo se puede usar la IA, y la conclusión sobre «reglas por materia»; ajustados «encargo» y las líneas de actuación a lo que dice la página; título de la fuente neutralizado.

Papel docente: titular y entradilla ya no hablan de debate «dividido» (las intervenciones coinciden); «jornada universitaria» a «jornada sobre IA y educación»; el dilema se presenta como recogido en una intervención.
Agentes de consola, MotionVideo y breve de Mollick: sin cambios de contenido, comprobados contra sus fuentes y mensajes.
